title: Frequently Asked Questions
text: Short answers to what people ask most before starting a project.

items.q: How long does it take to build a website or system?
items.a: Timing is agreed together once the requirements are clear. The main factors are the scope of work and how complete the material from you is. A simple website is usually quicker than a custom information system or dashboard, which is built in stages.

items.q: How much does a website or application cost?
items.a: Cost depends on your needs, features, and complexity. Once we understand what you need, we send a written estimate of cost and time before work starts.

items.q: Can you build a system or dashboard around our business workflow?
items.a: Yes, within the agreed scope. We build information systems, dashboards, and automation that follow your business workflow, including user management, access rights, and reports.

items.q: Does the website work well on phones?
items.a: Yes. Our websites and applications are designed mobile-first and responsive, and tested on several common screen sizes before release.

items.q: Who owns the domain and hosting?
items.a: We recommend registering the domain and hosting in your name so you stay in control. We help with the purchase, setup, and going live.

items.q: Is there support after the website is finished?
items.a: After release, we help resolve issues that come from our work within a period agreed together. Regular maintenance or further development is optional and discussed separately.
We apply security practices suited to the project, such as authentication, role-based access, and database security rules, to limit data access to authorized people.

items.q: What should we prepare before we talk?
items.a: Just a rough idea of your goals, who will use it, and reference examples if you have any. No concept yet is fine; we shape it together during the discussion.
The payment scheme is agreed at the start and put in writing. It is usually in stages: a down payment before work begins and the balance once the work is finished and approved.

items.q: Do we own the source code and design?
items.a: Rights to the deliverables, including code and design, are discussed and agreed before the project starts and put in a written agreement. Third-party services such as hosting or databases follow each provider's terms.
The number of revision rounds is agreed at the start according to the project scope. Changes outside the original scope are discussed separately and estimated before any work is done.

items.q: Are there monthly fees after the website is done?
items.a: Recurring costs are usually just the domain and hosting paid to the provider. Maintenance or further development is optional and agreed separately if you need it.
